subject: arts-music
lesson_title: Unit assessment: advanced performance, direction, and production
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Theatre — Performing
essential_question: What does it take to lead other people toward a shared interpretation?
learning_objectives: Demonstrate current mastery across advanced performance, direction, and production, showing process or evidence for each response.
Communicate understanding of advanced performance, direction, and production using subject-appropriate evidence or representation.
Check, revise, or improve the work on advanced performance, direction, and production against the stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task on advanced performance, direction, and production.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
materials: script, score, or devised material — public-domain or original only
private rehearsal space; no recording equipment is required at any point

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Mastery work on advanced performance, direction, and production. Mastery: organize events, marks, sounds, words, objects, or movements through advanced performance, direction, and production, then use observable evidence to explain or revise a learner-owned decision. Set a meaningful constraint and revise from self-run checks.
primary_task: Target for this assess session: Demonstrate current mastery across advanced performance, direction, and production, showing process or evidence for each response. Communicate understanding of advanced performance, direction, and production using subject-appropriate evidence or representation. Check, revise, or improve the work on advanced performance, direction, and production against the stated success criteria. Closing evidence check: Identify the item you are least confident about and say what would resolve it. 1. Independent evidence: With models and exact cues closed, produce fresh evidence of advanced performance, direction, and production. Complete the required artistic work independently and preserve enough process evidence for the rubric. 2. Self check: Check objective constraints first, then cite artistic evidence for each judgment-based criterion. Do not score similarity to a model, polish unrelated to the target, or personal taste. Your choices remain yours: Different medium, subject or source material, sequence, criterion to test, final revision choices are valid when the learner meets objective constraints and supports the result with evidence. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about advanced performance, direction, and production, and it belongs to "Advanced Performance, Direction, and Production", which also covers separate topics such as advanced interpretation and stylistic fluency. Close out with this check before you stop: Identify the item you are least confident about and say what would resolve it. At grade 11 the bar is independent work with sustained self-direction: you set the constraint, defend it, and revise on the evidence of your own checks rather than on being told to.
requirements: Independent evidence: With models and exact cues closed, produce fresh evidence of advanced performance, direction, and production. Complete the required artistic work independently and preserve enough process evidence for the rubric.

Authored success criteria for advanced performance, direction, and production: The learner completes the central task on advanced performance, direction, and production., The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer., and The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
Learner-owned choices during this unit assessment: medium, subject or source material, sequence, criterion to test, final revision.
deliverable: Independent evidence, Self check, with the observable Arts evidence and learner-owned decisions identified in each block.
critique_criteria: The submission contains fresh independent evidence; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.
The learner locates relevant sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.
The learner states an intent or claim and supports it with observable evidence while retaining ownership of artistic decisions.
The required fresh work was produced independently with models and exact cues closed, then checked against the stated criteria.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a written analysis, labelled plan, evidence table, notation, diagram, or private artifact check that preserves the stated target. No microphone, camera, recording, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries exactly the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording. A written or notated account of the intended performance is a full substitute.

This work spans sessions, so supply a written milestone plan, explicit checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown. Executive-function load — sequencing, holding the plan in mind, remembering where the work stopped — must not become a silent part of what is being assessed.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting advanced performance, direction, and production.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce advanced performance, direction, and production to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one sequence relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact sequence evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply advanced performance, direction, and production under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on advanced performance, direction, and production rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_registry.meaning: An artistic relationship can be tested across more than one medium when the same structure—such as repetition, contrast, or sequence—remains observable.
The relationship among artistic intent, observable sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent, and a criteria-based conclusion.

technique_registry.meaning: Isolate and test one sequence relationship while working on advanced performance, direction, and production.
Record observable evidence before judging, then choose or decline a revision with a reason.
Use a bounded study, loop, excerpt, map, or prototype to test one relationship without demanding polish.

age_policy.language: Advanced studio, rehearsal, analysis, and project language without unnecessary abstraction.
age_policy.safety: Use familiar low-risk materials, stop or adjust any physical or sound action that causes discomfort, and require adult help for cutting, heat, fumes, or heavy equipment.
age_policy.privacy: Private work and self-critique carry full credit; no public display, identifiable media, account, or recording is required.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for advanced performance, direction, and production is present, but the record does not yet locate sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
